solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Listen to the complete record; impartial judges must

definitions.meaning: a gramophone record has an A side and a B side, so listening to all of it means playing both
a fair judge weighs the case put by each party before deciding

explanation.walkthrough: The first definition is a literal reading about a vinyl record; the second is the idiom for fair-minded listening.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom for considering each party's argument is literally true of playing both faces of a disc.

clue.text: Tail one wags in delight

indicators.note: a tail that wags moves to and fro, so the letters of the two words are shaken into a new order

explanation.surface: A happy dog wags its tail in delight.
explanation.walkthrough: 'wags' rearranges TAILONE into the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Both words name a state of great happiness or joy; a straightforward synonym.

clue.text: One in race to destruction

indicators.note: the word in says the numeral for one is placed within the word for race

parts.note: to run is to race, and a run is a race
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: Someone racing headlong towards their own downfall.
explanation.definitionFit: A synonym: ruin means utter destruction or collapse.

clue.text: Large volume of transport?

definitions.meaning: an ... edition is a big book collecting several works
the full old name for a bus, a means of public transport

explanation.surface: A query about how much traffic there is.
explanation.definitionFit: Omnibus means both a collected book edition and, in full form, a passenger bus.

clue.text: Sea bed?

parts.note: not the ocean floor but a swinging bed slung between hooks on which sailors slept at sea

explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests the floor of the ocean; the question mark invites reading it as a sailor's bed aboard ship.
explanation.definitionFit: A canvas sling bed was the traditional sleeping place for sailors aboard ship.

clue.text: This month in Westminster

indicators.note: the word in says the letters sit inside the name Westminster

explanation.surface: Something happening in Parliament this month.
explanation.walkthrough: INST is an old business-letter abbreviation for instant, meaning of the current month.
explanation.definitionFit: The abbreviation for instant, a formal term used in correspondence to mean the current month.

clue.text: Broken-hearted, but protected from shock

indicators.note: something broken is in pieces, so the letters of hearted are reassembled differently

explanation.surface: Someone heartbroken yet emotionally shielded from further shock.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Broken' looks like part of 'Broken-hearted', but it is the anagram signal working on 'hearted'. The shock is electrical.
explanation.definitionFit: An earthed appliance is connected to ground so that it cannot give an electric shock.

clue.text: Magazine articles that could do a lot of damage

definitions.text: Magazine articles that could do a lot of damage

parts.words: Magazine articles that could do a lot of damage
parts.note: a magazine here is an ammunition store, and its articles are the explosive charge and projectiles for old firearms

explanation.walkthrough: Magazine suggests a periodical with damaging stories, but it is an arms store.
explanation.definitionFit: Gunpowder and lead balls were the ammunition kept in an armoury's store for muskets and cannon.

clue.text: Not everyone sees the fun in this party game

definitions.text: Not everyone sees the fun in this party game

parts.words: Not everyone sees the fun in this party game
parts.note: in this game one player is blindfolded and so literally cannot see the fun

explanation.walkthrough: 'Not everyone sees the fun' sounds like a remark about humour, but in this game the blindfolded player really cannot see.
explanation.definitionFit: A traditional children's party game in which a blindfolded player tries to catch the others.

clue.text: Speech from 'Love on the Dole'?

parts.note: love means zero in tennis scoring, written as the letter O
a dole is a portion handed out, a ration

explanation.surface: A speech taken from a novel about unemployment.
explanation.walkthrough: Love on the Dole is a 1933 novel by Walter Greenwood about poverty in northern England; 'the dole' is British slang for unemployment benefit, but here dole means a share.
explanation.definitionFit: An oration is a formal speech delivered on a ceremonial occasion; a synonym.

clue.text: Poor visibility — beginnings of rain and light wind

parts.note: mist reduces how far one can see

indicators.note: beginnings means the opening letters of the three following words

explanation.surface: A weather report: low visibility, the start of rain and a gentle breeze.
explanation.walkthrough: 'light wind' reads as a breeze, but 'light' is fodder and 'wind' alone defines.
explanation.definitionFit: The mistral is a strong cold northerly wind blowing down the Rhône valley in southern France.

clue.text: Work at home? It's murder!

parts.note: to do is to work or carry out a task
in means at home, as in staying in

explanation.surface: Someone complaining that working from home is a nightmare.
explanation.walkthrough: 'It's murder!' looks like an exclamation of hardship, but 'murder' is the definition as a verb.
explanation.definitionFit: The informal phrasal verb means to kill someone.

clue.text: Cleric who may have a prior appointment

definitions.text: Cleric who may have a prior appointment

parts.words: Cleric who may have a prior appointment
parts.note: a prior is a monk ranking just below the head of an abbey, who may appoint him

explanation.walkthrough: 'a prior appointment' sounds like a clash in the diary; here a prior is a monastic office.
explanation.definitionFit: The head of an abbey of monks, who ranks above the prior.

clue.text: The point to make next

parts.note: taken as written
N, north, is a point of the compass

explanation.surface: Advice about what argument to raise next.
explanation.definitionFit: Then and next both mean afterwards, following in sequence; synonyms.

clue.text: The last competitors try to be first in this event

definitions.text: The last competitors try to be first in this event

parts.words: The last competitors try to be first in this event
parts.note: in a team race each runner hands on the baton, so the final leg runners aim to cross the line first

explanation.walkthrough: The 'last competitors' are not losers but the anchor runners of each team.
explanation.definitionFit: A team race in which members run successive legs, passing a baton.

clue.text: Getting horse into ship poses unexpected difficulties

indicators.note: into says the word for horse goes inside the abbreviation for ship

parts.note: SS stands for steamship
a nag is an old or poor horse

explanation.surface: Loading a horse onto a ship proves trickier than expected.
explanation.definitionFit: Snags are hitches or unforeseen obstacles; a synonym.

clue.text: Athletes naturally full of beans?

definitions.meaning: runner beans are a variety of climbing bean, so these plants are full of beans by nature

explanation.surface: Sportspeople who are always energetic.
explanation.walkthrough: 'full of beans' means lively, but here it is literal: runner beans are a common British garden vegetable.
explanation.definitionFit: Racers on foot, and climbing bean plants grown in British gardens.

clue.text: Brunel's realm?

definitions.meaning: Isambard ... Brunel was the great Victorian engineer, and this was his middle name
a country ruled by a monarch

explanation.surface: The domain of a famous engineer.
explanation.walkthrough: Isambard Kingdom Brunel built the Great Western Railway and the Clifton Suspension Bridge in Britain.
explanation.definitionFit: A realm is a territory ruled by a king or queen; also Brunel's middle name.

clue.text: The last place a Buddhist wants to go

definitions.text: The last place a Buddhist wants to go

parts.words: The last place a Buddhist wants to go
parts.note: the idiom suggests somewhere dreaded, but literally it is the final state of enlightenment a Buddhist seeks

explanation.walkthrough: 'The last place someone wants to go' normally means a place they want to avoid; here it is the ultimate goal.
explanation.definitionFit: In Buddhism, the final release from the cycle of rebirth and suffering.

clue.text: Arch is rough cast on the outside

indicators.note: on the outside says the rearranged letters wrap around the word is
to cast is to throw or mould anew, so the letters of rough are reshaped

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: An archway is roughly rendered on its exterior.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Arch' looks like a curved structure but is an adjective here, as in an arch smile or knowing look.
explanation.definitionFit: Arch, as an adjective, means playfully mischievous or knowing, as roguish does.

clue.text: Garments appear dishevelled on student

indicators.note: in a down clue, on means placed beneath, so the student comes after
dishevelled means untidy, so the letters of appear are disordered

parts.note: L is the learner plate on a British learner driver's car

explanation.surface: A student's clothes look scruffy.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down entry 'on' means placed below, so the student's letter follows the rearranged word.
explanation.definitionFit: Apparel is a collective word for clothing; garments is a plural synonym.

clue.text: Diet for the troops lacks tea, say

indicators.note: lacks says a letter is missing from the word for the troops

parts.note: a regiment is a body of troops

indicators.note: say signals that the word tea is spoken, giving the letter of the same sound

parts.note: the drink, whose name is pronounced like a letter of the alphabet

explanation.surface: Army rations come without a cup of tea.
explanation.definitionFit: A regimen is a prescribed course of diet or exercise; a synonym.

clue.text: Fruit of theatrical conversation

definitions.meaning: a stalk eaten stewed like fruit in desserts
actors in crowd scenes mutter this word to sound like background chatter

explanation.surface: Something fruity said on stage.
explanation.definitionFit: A tart pink stalk used as a dessert fruit, and the word extras mumble to imitate crowd noise.

clue.text: New moral we found in old writer

indicators.note: new means the letters of moral and we are arranged afresh

explanation.surface: An old author found a fresh moral lesson.
explanation.walkthrough: Christopher Marlowe was an Elizabethan playwright.
explanation.definitionFit: Christopher Marlowe was an English dramatist of the sixteenth century, an example of an old writer.

clue.text: Make one's name as a writer

definitions.text: Make one's name as a writer

parts.words: Make one's name as a writer
parts.note: sounds like becoming a famous author, but means putting one's own name in ink on a document

explanation.walkthrough: 'Make one's name' usually means become famous; here it means literally writing one's name.
explanation.definitionFit: To put one's autograph on a letter or contract in ink.

clue.text: It may be smoked out of its den

definitions.text: It may be smoked out of its den

parts.words: It may be smoked out of its den
parts.note: suggests an animal driven from its lair by smoke, but means a drug smoked in a den

explanation.walkthrough: 'smoked out of its den' sounds like flushing a fox from its lair; the den is a place where a narcotic is smoked.
explanation.definitionFit: A narcotic from poppies traditionally smoked in dens set aside for that purpose.

clue.text: Lacking lustre, sailor is after doctor

indicators.note: is after says the sailor follows the doctor

parts.note: AB, able-bodied seaman, is a sailor

explanation.surface: A dull sailor chases a doctor.
explanation.definitionFit: Drab means dull and colourless, without brightness; a synonym.

clue.text: Fruit attached to the trunk

definitions.meaning: the red berries of the wild rose
the joints where the legs meet the torso

explanation.surface: Fruit growing on a tree trunk.
explanation.definitionFit: Rose berries, and the body parts joining legs to torso.

clue.text: Storage for crude oils

indicators.note: crude means rough or unrefined, so the letters of oils are roughly rearranged

explanation.surface: A tank for storing unrefined oil.
explanation.walkthrough: 'crude oils' reads as petroleum; 'crude' is the anagram signal.
explanation.definitionFit: A silo is a tower or pit for storing grain or other material, so it is a storage structure.

clue.text: Famous actor I observed in a musical

indicators.note: observed in says the letter is seen within the musical's title

parts.note: Oliver! is Lionel Bart's musical based on Oliver Twist

explanation.surface: Seeing a celebrated actor in a stage musical.
explanation.walkthrough: Laurence Olivier was a celebrated English stage and film actor.
explanation.definitionFit: Laurence Olivier was one of the most renowned British actors, an example of a famous actor.

clue.text: Substandard may mean a small reduction in price

definitions.meaning: informally, not quite right or acceptable
a little taken off the price

explanation.surface: Damaged goods may be sold slightly cheaper.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase means both not up to the mark and a little discount.

clue.text: One who informs a referee?

definitions.meaning: someone who exposes wrongdoing in an organisation
a football referee blows a whistle to stop play

explanation.surface: Someone who tells tales to the match official.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone exposing wrongdoing, and literally an official who blows a whistle.
